situation (example wording): "murders by state in 2024", "Murder rates 1960 to 2024, broken down by all 50 states", "trends in murder by state" (a Part I crime, or violent or property crime, for every state)
what the app does today: Asked which place, or declined "This kind of answer doesn't list every place".
proposed behavior: A Part I crime, or violent or property crime, by state (also said "for each state", "for every state", "in all 50 states", "per state", "state by state") comes from Crime Index's state figures: the 50 states, from 1960, without the District of Columbia. One year is the table State | figure, highest first. Years named, or a trend with none, is one long table State | Year | figure, ordered by state and year, with no chart (over a thousand rows). No year and no trend is every year by year, the long table (P181, which supersedes the ask). A detail only NIBRS records (a weapon, a drug, carjacking) by state keeps today's handling.
exact default or choices offered: One year: State | figure. Years named or a trend: State | Year | figure, no chart. No year: every year by year (P181).
why: Jeff 2026-11-16 (through the coordinator): "long table State | Year | Rate when the span is named (chart off); a single year gets the plain State | Rate table."
